title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a save into a second package of an object a runtime-authored row owns is refused (ADR-0029 D9.9)
body:
Fixes #23416
Clause-②: no

## What this does

`classifyObjectContribution` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) asked the registry one question, `getPackagedObjectOwner`, which answers for a CODE artifact only. An object that package P's `sys_metadata` row created at runtime has no packaged owner, so a save of it naming package Q classified as `own` and was written. The write-through then called `registerObject(…, Q, …, 'own')`, the registry's single-owner rule (ADR-0029 D3) refused it, and `applyObjectRegistryMutation`'s best-effort `console.warn` swallowed the refusal. The save answered `200` while `sys_metadata` held a Q-bound row the registry could not hold: the disagreement ADR-0029 D9.9 (`overlayPackageMismatchError`) exists to prevent.

The classifier now asks one more question when there is no packaged owner: the registry's own `own` contributor (`getObjectOwner(name)`, keyed on the object name exactly as `registerObject` keys its contributors). When that owner is bound to a real package and the row's binding names a different package, it answers the existing `mismatch` arm. So the save door refuses with the code-owner path's refusal and prescription (`OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / `422`), before `ensureOverlayIndex` and every `put`. One arm answers both owners; no second refusal path, no new error code, no new message.

Unchanged by construction:

- A binding equal to the owner's package: `own`, an ordinary re-registration (the owner's re-save stays `200`).
- A save naming no package: still `own`. A direct publish-mode save naming no package is addressed to the owner's row before this runs (`packagelessAddress`).
- An owner keyed by the `sys_metadata` sentinel (a package-less runtime object) or by no package: left to today's verdict. It names no package the prescription could direct a save to. See the acceptance notes.
- A code-packaged owner: the existing table, untouched.

## Premise check (the seat's ruling premise)

The ruling needed a runtime owner's package that can be read deterministically at that point of `saveMetaItem`. It holds. The registry keeps exactly one `own` contributor per object name (`registerObject` enforces it), and that contributor is the very fact `registerObject` judges an incoming `own` claim against. The arm predicts the registry's own refusal and judges nothing else. The object write-through is not kernel-gated (`applyRegistryWriteThrough`'s object branch), so every saved runtime object is in the registry on every kernel topology. Measured at the HTTP door on both topologies (below).

## Measured before the fix (real kernel, base `cb9841aa25`)

`ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + an in-memory driver, `saveMetaItem` as `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?package=Q` calls it:

| setup | Q's save | rows stored | registry owner | warn |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| P saved `qa_probe_gadget` | `success: true`, "Saved object 'qa_probe_gadget' (env-wide, package=com.qa.q, state=active)" | `com.qa.p`, `com.qa.q` | `com.qa.p` | `registerObject failed … already owned by package "com.qa.p" … cannot claim ownership` |

## Measured after the fix

- Real kernel pin (new file, 4 cases): Q's save answers `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / `422` (with `packageId` Q and `ownerPackageId` P). No row and no history entry is stored for Q. The registry and `sys_metadata` both still say P. CONTROLS: P's own re-save answers success and the registry follows it; a save naming no package addresses P's row; a code-packaged owner answers `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / `403`, as it did before this change (measured on the base).
- HTTP door, one-time reading (the real `RestServer` `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name` route over a real better-sqlite3 engine, control-plane and environment kernels): P `200`; Q `422` with body `code: OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` and the D9.9 sentence; P again `200`; stored bindings `[com.probe.p]`.
- Other faces of the same door, one-time readings on the real kernel, before → after:
  - a draft save into Q: success with a Q draft row stored → `422`, no draft row;
  - `duplicatePackage` P → Q of an object whose name lacks P's namespace prefix (so the copy keeps the name): listed in `copied` with a Q row the registry never held → listed in `failed` with the D9.9 text, nothing stored;
  - boot (`loadMetaFromDb`) with a stored Q row beside P's: P registered and the Q row counted in `errors` either way. The warn line changes from `code=OBJECT_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT` to `code=OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH`.

## Fixtures re-judged (the rule's consumer radius)

Two suites built the two-package runtime shape by saving the second package's row through the door. Both are RE-SEEDED, not weakened: the first package's row is still saved through the door, and the second row is written straight into the store, as a row stored before this refusal existed.

- `packages/objectql/src/protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts`, `twoPackageObject` (PR #23408's pin, per pointer `6163309335`). The seeded row is the first row's own shape, rebound and re-labelled, with the repository's checksum (`hashSpec`). The fixture asserts that formula on the row the door just wrote, and that the registry still holds the first package.
- `packages/rest/src/meta-delete-drop-storage-other-rows.test.ts`, `twoPackageObject` (PR #23464's pin, landed after the claim). Its existing `seedUnboundRow` is generalised to `seedStoredRow(packageId)`. This file is a **surface increment** over the claim's declared surface: it is the PM's swept consumer radius, and the PR breaks it without the re-seed.

Each re-seeded fixture was ablated against the behaviour it pins, to show it still bites (mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, `dist/` proven by `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`, restored blob equal to `HEAD` and the tree clean):

| ablation | mutated | restored |
|:--|:--|:--|
| this PR's arm (`mismatch` return replaced by `own`), new pin | 1 failed / 3 passed (the refusal case: "expected null to be an instance of Error") | 4 passed |
| #23408's heal (its remaining-rows branch made unreachable), heal file | 5 failed / 10 passed (the four re-seeded object cases + the dashboard case) | 15 passed |
| #23464's drop refusal (its remaining-rows check made unreachable), rest file | 3 failed / 2 passed | 5 passed |

| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` | exit 0 |

| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (tsc + `check:test-typecheck`) | exit 0 · the test layer compiles, debt unchanged |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` | exit 0 · 283 files · 5852 tests passed, 326 skipped (first attempt: lock exit 99, re-run with the same slot) |

The objectql suite's `repo` project, which holds the tests that read outside the package, is CI's (`test:repo`). The red-before reading for the new pin was taken at the base: 2 failed of 4. The refusal case answered `null` (a success). The code-owner control then read `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, and that measured value is what the control now pins.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `55bb8619e7`: 67 commands. All 67 ran at that head with exit codes recorded, and `--ran` reconciles: "67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". Every command exited 0. `check:type-check-debt` first got lock exit 99 (its own PREREQUISITE NOT MET, exit 3) and passed when re-run under the lock: "1 ledger entr(ies) re-measured … none above its recorded number". On an earlier head, `check-adr-0087-registration` refused a `## FROM → TO` section label beside `no-migration-prescription`. The changeset now states the FROM/TO as request answers, and the gate passes (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).

CI owns everything the derivation does not place: the artifact-roster families, the wide-population families, the type-check lanes, Test Core, Build Core, dogfood and the temporal conformance job. `packages/runtime` and `packages/qa/dogfood` suites were not run locally. A heuristic sweep of their tests for a second package's object save through the door found none.

`origin/main` has moved past `394f65e89` by two commits (`ad5a7d7c39` spec page-action rows, `111b5821ce` a runtime test). Neither touches this diff's packages or behaviour; CI's merge ref covers them.

## Acceptance notes

- **Package-less owner, same family, not fixed here.** An object a row bound to NO package owns (`sys_metadata` sentinel) behaves as this card did before the fix. On a real kernel at `cb9841aa25`, a package-less save then a `?package=Q` save answered success with rows `[null, com.qa.q]`, while the registry kept the sentinel owner and warned `already owned by package "sys_metadata"`. The arm deliberately excludes it: the D9.9 prescription would tell the author to bind to `'sys_metadata'`, which is not a package, and the right remedy (orphan adoption, or saving without a package) is a wording decision. Reported to the seat for the D9.9 family's close-out, not filed by this PR.
- **`duplicatePackage` now reports what it used to fake.** A source object whose name lacks the source namespace prefix keeps its name in the copy. Before this PR that copy was a row the registry refused, over the same physical table (object name = table name). Now it lands in `failed[]`. The docblock of `duplicatePackage` already calls a same-name copy a collision. The prescription text it carries ("bind … to P, or have Q extend") is the code-owner path's and fits the save door better than the duplicate face; renaming the object is the remedy there.
- **The prescription's second remedy is a code-package affordance.** "have Q extend the object instead" names `objectExtensions`, which a code package declares. No runtime metadata door authors an extension. The ruled prescription is reused unchanged; the first remedy (bind to P) is always available.
- **Callers left as they are.** `applyObjectRegistryMutation` and `loadMetaFromDb` already route a `mismatch` to their warn and per-record `errors`. The heal comment in `restoreArtifactRegistryView` ("a second package's runtime-authored row never registered (its write-through was refused at save)") stays true of stored rows and sits in the delete heal that `deleteMetaItem` runs, outside this card's surface.
